series: Things Living In Your House, Part 14
sources: Penn State Extension, Fruit Flies: attracted to ripened fruits and vegetables; infestations often begin with overripe produce brought into the home, since eggs may already be on it; a female can lay about 500 eggs; the life cycle from egg to adult can be completed in about a week; control by removing ripe produce and using cider-vinegar traps; https://extension.psu.edu/fruit-flies

University of Kentucky Entomology, Fruit Flies (Ent-621): fruit flies are attracted to fermenting fruit; development from egg to adult takes about 8-10 days; traps of apple cider vinegar; refrigerate ripe produce; https://entomology.ca.uky.edu/ef621

NASA History, A Brief History of Animals in Space: the first animals deliberately sent into space were fruit flies, launched aboard a US V-2 rocket on 20 February 1947; the capsule was recovered with the flies alive; https://history.nasa.gov/animals.html

Reiter et al. 2001, Genome Research, A systematic analysis of human disease-associated gene sequences in Drosophila melanogaster: about 77% of human disease genes examined had a recognizable match in the fruit fly; https://genome.cshlp.org/content/11/6/1114

Nobel Prize: Thomas Hunt Morgan (1933, studied Drosophila from about 1910); Lewis, Nüsslein-Volhard and Wieschaus (1995); Hoffmann (2011); Hall, Rosbash and Young (2017) for fruit fly research; https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/

Fruit fly flight: Drosophila beat their wings about 200 times per second; compound eyes of about 700-800 facets (ommatidia) with red pigment (e.g. Dickinson lab, Caltech; FlyBase); https://www.dickinsonlab.caltech.edu/

title: The Fly in Your Fruit Bowl Went to Space Before Humans Did 🍌

beats.say: That fruit fly? It probably rode home on your bananas.
The fruit fly. About the size of a sesame seed.
Its eggs often ride in on the fruit itself.
Outside, it lives on ripe, rotting fruit.
It follows the smell of fermenting fruit.
One female can lay about five hundred eggs.
In about ten days, the babies are adults.
Your fruit bowl is a fly nursery.
But this tiny fly is also a science hero.
Scientists have studied it for over a hundred years.
Most human disease genes have a match in it.
Fruit fly research has won several Nobel Prizes.
And in 1947, fruit flies rode a rocket into space.
The first animals ever sent up there.
And they came back alive.
So I shrank down to meet one.
Its eyes are red, and made of hundreds of lenses.
Its wings beat about two hundred times a second.
Want them gone? Fill a jar with cider vinegar.
Add a drop of dish soap. They fall in, and sink.
And keep ripe fruit in the fridge.
Would you still eat that banana?
The smallest pest in your kitchen beat humans to space.
